simple: A `ViewportFrame` is a little window in your UI that shows real 3D objects. It uses its own camera to take a live picture of whatever models you put inside it. You can use it for a minimap, a spinning sword in an inventory, or a preview of what a player has equipped. You can make the object follow your camera, stay still, or spin, and even add shiny sky reflections.
analogy: A viewport frame is like a TV screen in your menu, showing what a little camera inside a tiny studio is filming.
keyPoints: A `ViewportFrame` shows 3D objects inside flat 2D UI using a camera.
Objects you want to see must be placed inside the `ViewportFrame`, not just in Workspace.
Set the frame's `CurrentCamera` to choose which camera it looks through.
To make the view move with the player's camera, set `CurrentCamera` to the main `Camera`.
For a still view, duplicate the camera, point it where you want, and use the copy as `CurrentCamera`.
To make an object spin, move the viewport camera around it in a script every frame.
Lighting inside is set by `Ambient`, `LightDirection`, and `LightColor`; `ImageColor3` and `ImageTransparency` tint and fade the whole view.
A `Sky` placed inside the frame can give shiny parts reflections.

terms.viewport: A window that shows a view of 3D things.
terms.render: To draw something on the screen.
terms.CurrentCamera: The camera the `ViewportFrame` looks through. Without one, it shows nothing.
terms.static: Not moving. A static view always looks the same.
terms.cubemap: Six pictures (front, back, left, right, up, down) wrapped around like a box, used to make reflections.
terms.Field of view: How wide the camera sees, in degrees. A smaller number zooms in; a bigger number shows more.
terms.CFrame: A value holding both a position and a rotation. `CFrame.new(0, 0, 10)` means 10 studs back along the Z axis from the center.
terms.LightDirection: Which way the light shines. The default (-1, -1, -1) points down, left, and forward from the center.

example.title: Spin an item in an inventory slot
example.place: LocalScript inside a ViewportFrame (inside a ScreenGui in StarterGui), with a Part placed inside the ViewportFrame
example.code:
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local viewportFrame = script.Parent

local cameraDistance = 10 -- studs from the object
local spinSpeed = 50 -- degrees per second

-- Make a camera just for this frame
local viewportCamera = Instance.new("Camera")
viewportCamera.FieldOfView = 50
viewportFrame.CurrentCamera = viewportCamera
viewportCamera.Parent = viewportFrame

local object = viewportFrame:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("BasePart")
if object then
	-- Put the object at the center
	object.CFrame = CFrame.new(0, 0, 0)

	local t = 0
	RunService.PostSimulation:Connect(function(deltaTime)
		t += deltaTime
		-- Turn around the center, then step back 10 studs to look at it
		viewportCamera.CFrame = CFrame.Angles(0, math.rad(t * spinSpeed), 0) * CFrame.new(0, 0, cameraDistance)
	end)
else
	warn("Put a part inside the ViewportFrame")
end
explain: We make a new `Camera` and tell the `ViewportFrame` to look through it.
We find the first part inside the frame and put it at the center (0, 0, 0).
Every frame, `PostSimulation` gives us the time passed, which we add to `t`.
We spin the camera around the center by `t * spinSpeed` degrees and move it 10 studs back, so it circles the part and the part looks like it is spinning.

watchOut: Moving a part out of Workspace into the `ViewportFrame` removes it from the world. Duplicate it first if you still need it in the game.
If the frame is blank, check that `CurrentCamera` is set and the camera is pointed at the object.
To change the view, move the camera, not the objects inside the frame.
Objects inside a `ViewportFrame` do not act like physical things in the world; it is just a picture.
